name: Stack to overload
summary: Several allied weapons feed one meter on an enemy vehicle: each hit adds a stack of charge, and every stack hampers it a little more (in Tempest Rising, slower movement and fire). When the stacks are full the charge tips over into an overload: the vehicle burns, crawls and can't use its abilities. Finisher weapons destroy an overloaded vehicle outright, whatever its health, so builders lay the stacks and a finisher cashes them in. Soldiers, buildings and specially shielded vehicles are immune. It is a variant of freeze-and-shatter: unlike a freeze, the overloaded vehicle can still crawl and fire slowly while it burns and loses its abilities, the stacks ride on ordinary damaging weapons, and only designated finisher weapons cash them in.
counterplay: Break contact while the meter fills: an overload needs many hits, so a vehicle that pulls back or puts cover between itself and the builders early never reaches it.
Hunt the builders: without stacks the finisher is an ordinary gun, and the Voltaic Tank lays no charge of its own.
Keep away from the finisher while overloaded: the overload alone only burns and slows, and only a finisher weapon turns it into an instant kill.
Field units the charge can't touch: soldiers, buildings and harvesters are immune to Tempest Charge, Tempest Shielded vehicles ignore both stages, and Reliable Systems vehicles ignore the overload.
Spread out: the Voltaic beam arcs to vehicles packed close around its target, so a tight column hands it several victims.
Attack the finisher from the air: the Voltaic Tank's cannon can't fire at aircraft.

other_examples.unit: Tempest Charge builders and Tempest Overflow (Matchstick, Machinist, Trebuchet and others)
other_examples.note: The builders of the Voltaic Tank's combo. Weapons with the Tempest Charge passive add a stack to each enemy vehicle or aircraft they hit: among them the Matchstick's grenade launcher, the Machinist's Searchlight Sensor, Trebuchet shells, Condor bombs and the Hijacker's grenades; ground vehicles also gain stacks in Tempest fields, and the Cultivator charges every enemy vehicle around it. Each of the five stacks slows movement and attacks, and after the fifth the vehicle falls into Overflow: it takes damage over time, is slowed much more and can't use abilities. Some Veti weapons instead deal extra damage to charged targets (Tempest Affinity). The GDF Sniper's shot from stealth and the Instability Missile inflict Overflow directly, and Voltaic Reaction weapons (the Operative, the Voltaic Railgun and the Machinist's Tempest Arc besides the tank) destroy Overflowing vehicles at once. Infantry, buildings and harvesters never take the charge; Tempest Shielded units are immune to both stages and Reliable Systems units to Overflow, while the Tempest Sphere's plating spends the charge to repair itself.

sources.title: Ability, Tempest Rising Wiki
sources.note: Its Voltaic Reaction list names the Operative, Voltaic Tank, Voltaic Railgun and the Machinist's Tempest Arc.

other_examples.note: Status damage fills separate meters under a unit's health bar. EMP damage is weighed against the target's current health and adds up from every hit; once the meter is full the unit is stunned and can't move, shoot or use abilities until the meter drains back below full, which it does at a steady rate. Each EMP weapon can push the meter only so far past full, which caps how long it can hold a target down. Disarm damage fills its own meter and silences weapons and abilities while leaving the unit free to move, and slow damage cuts speed and rate of fire by up to a half. Because the meters stack, several EMP units firing together fill one far sooner.

sources.title: Status Effects, Zero-K Wiki
sources.note: The wiki on the game's own site.

other_examples.note: From patch 7.20 until 7.36 the curse counted Abaddon's hits on an enemy: each one slowed it, and the fourth turned the slow into a curse that silenced it and slowed it harder (from 7.35 the curse also hurt it over time), while every allied hero who struck the cursed target attacked faster. Each hit restarted the counter's timer, so the hits only had to come a few seconds apart, and from 7.28 until 7.31 an upgrade let two of his spells add a hit to every enemy they struck. Patch 7.36 dropped the counter and the silence: now each of his attacks applies the slow and the damage over time at once, and allies who hit the target still gain attack speed.

shooter_analogues.note: Solar abilities and weapons scorch their targets with damage over time that grows as more stacks pile on. When a target reaches a hundred stacks it ignites: a large Solar blast that hurts everything around it and stuns Unstoppable Champions. Some tools set off an ignition sooner, such as the Titan's Consecration slam, which ignites any scorched target its wave reaches, and the Hunter's Gunpowder Gamble explosive, which ignites when shot in mid-air. One Ember fragment makes each ignition spread scorch to the targets it catches, so one ignition can start the next.

shooter_analogues.game: extra:Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon
shooter_analogues.note: Every hit strains the target's Attitude Control System by an amount set by the weapon's Impact and the target's Attitude Stability; when enough hits land in a short time the system overloads, and the staggered machine is open to punishment for a moment, taking extra Direct Hit damage from whatever strikes it then. Both steady streams of fire and single heavy blows fill the gauge, each weapon by its own amount, and the makers' own example opens with machine guns and a missile volley to stagger the target, then follows with a pulse blade. Any machine can be staggered, from small mechs to the largest bosses.

sources.title: Armored Core VI Fires of Rubicon launches August 25 - New gameplay details, PlayStation.Blog
sources.note: Interview with the developers on Sony's PlayStation Blog, before release.

shooter_analogues.note: In the tabletop game a flamer does almost nothing to 'Mechs and vehicles beyond heating them up. In MechWarrior Online a 'Mech whose heat passes its threshold overheats and shuts down, and the flamer adds heat to its target, but only up to nine tenths of that threshold, so flamers alone never force the shutdown: the rest has to come from heat the target makes itself.

sources.title: Heat Sinks, MechWarrior Online Wiki
sources.note: Defines the heat threshold at which a 'Mech overheats and shuts down.

shooter_analogues.note: Blast weapons build up blastblight on a monster with each hit, and changing colours tell the hunters how close the next blast is. At the threshold an explosion deals a set amount of damage to the part that took the last hit, the build-up starts again from nothing, and the monster's tolerance rises, so each later blast takes more hits. Hunters who catch blastblight from a monster explode when struck, or soon anyway, unless they roll a few times to clear it.

sources.title: Status Effects, Monster Hunter Wiki
sources.version: Monster Hunter 4 onwards; Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate named it Slimeblight

player_translation.summary: A team combo for T2 and T3 cards. Builder weapons add a charge pip to every enemy vehicle they hit, and each pip slows it a little. At five pips the vehicle overloads for a few seconds: it burns, crawls and loses its ability keys, and a finisher weapon on another card hits it for heavy bonus damage. The victim sees the pips filling and can break contact, is briefly immune after an overload, and their team can hunt the builders or the finisher.
as_user: As a builder you buy a card whose main weapon also charges vehicles, such as a grenade launcher, a sensor gun or artillery shells. Every hit adds a pip on top of normal damage; your job is to tip enemy tanks into overload just as your finisher arrives.

As a finisher you carry a slow, heavy gun that does fair damage to anything and a crushing hit to an overloaded vehicle. You watch the pips over enemy vehicles and time your shot for the overload, like the Voltaic Tank winding up its beam.
Several builders on one tank fill it fast; one builder alone takes long enough that the target can react, so you play as a group.
The ping is the teamwork: an overload with no finisher nearby still burns and slows, but the kill is wasted, so call 'overloaded' and pull your finisher in.
The charge does nothing to soldiers, buildings or immune vehicles, so read the enemy line-up before you buy.
as_target: Sparking pips appear over your vehicle and on your HUD, with a crackle that grows louder; each one slows your driving and your rate of fire a little. Break contact, pop smoke or kill a builder before the fifth.
Overloaded, you burn, crawl and lose your ability keys for a few seconds, shown by heavy sparks and a countdown ring; your guns still fire, slowly.
The real danger is the finisher: back away from it, put a wall between you, or get a teammate onto it before it fires.
Hold F, the universal shake-off, to vent pips faster while nothing is hitting you; after an overload ends you can't gain pips for a short while, shown by a white outline.
teammates: The builders' team: two or three cards with charging weapons and one finisher form the combo; the builders call targets and the finisher closes in for the overload.
The victim's team: kill the builders or the finisher, body-block the overloaded ally, and bring units the charge can't touch, such as soldiers or shielded vehicles.
A teammate's repair tool clears pips from an ally's vehicle (but not a running overload), which gives the victim's team a rescue.
The finisher's arcs punish vehicles that bunch up, so the victim's team should spread out when a finisher is on the field.
controls: Builders: no extra key. Charging is a passive on the main weapon (left mouse) and uses the card's one passive slot; variants put a charging grenade or a charge pulse on Q, one counted key.
Finisher: the bonus against overloaded vehicles is a passive on the main weapon, also with no key; the variant that does both jobs puts its finisher shot on Q.
Middle mouse, the universal ping, on a charged or overloaded vehicle: 'charged, finish it'.
Victim: hold F to vent pips while out of fire; it never cancels a running overload. Teammates clear pips with the main fire of a repair tool.
feedback: Pips: up to five sparks circling the vehicle and pips on its health bar, visible to everyone, with colour and crackle rising at each pip.
Overload: heavy red arcs over the model, a countdown ring and a buzzing loop; the overloaded player's ability icons grey out and the screen edge flickers.
Finisher hit: a sharp crack and a bright flash, a large damage number, and a kill-feed icon that names the builders as well as the finisher.
Immune targets flash a small shield symbol when a charging weapon hits them, so players learn at once that the charge does nothing there.
The immunity window after an overload shows as a white outline on the vehicle.
changes_from_rts: In Tempest Rising a finisher kills an overloaded vehicle outright, whatever its health. Against a player that deletes the most expensive unit on the field in one hit, so the default finisher deals a heavy bonus hit and the outright kill is a high-spice variant.

The Tempest Rising pages describe no immunity after an Overflow; players need a short immunity window, or rising tolerance as Monster Hunter uses, so one team can't keep a tank locked out of its abilities.
Tempest fields charge any ground vehicle that drives through them. Fields are a map feature, so the card keeps only the weapons and leaves fields to a map variant or the charge-field variant.

An RTS shows stacks as small icons; a top-down shooter needs big pips over the vehicle and a HUD meter for the victim, plus a way to vent them (hold F), or the card carries the 'control without escape' balance flag.
Builders get assist credit for each overload they fed, so the players who did the work share the kill with the finisher.

team_play.notes: The team version of setup-and-finisher: the builders and the finisher are usually different players, several builders stack on one target, and the victim's team answers by venting or repairing pips, hunting the finisher or fielding units the charge can't touch.

notes: One stack counter per target, shared by every builder on a team, with a drain rate, a cap on how fast pips can be added and an overload timer.
The overload must slow movement and fire and block abilities in every system (seats, deploys, transforms), then end cleanly and start the immunity window.
The finisher's bonus needs one server-side rule for which hit counts, so two finishers never both claim the kill.
Immunity flags (soldiers, buildings, shielded vehicles), pip clearing by repair tools and assist credit for every builder add edge cases.
Pips must be readable from a top-down camera at a glance, for both teams.

An outright kill on any overloaded vehicle turns five hits and one finisher into a death sentence for a tank; the Voltaic Tank's own record notes that its makers toned down massed Voltaic Tanks in patch 1.6.0.
Many cheap builders can fill a meter almost at once; cap the pip rate, as Zero-K caps how far each EMP weapon can push its meter.
Chained overloads keep a vehicle without abilities for a long time; an immunity window or rising tolerance prevents it.
Soldiers being immune makes the pattern dead weight against infantry-heavy teams, so a card with it needs a useful base weapon.
Players must tell charge pips from other status icons, and an overload from a freeze or a stun.
Overloaded players need to see which enemy can finish them, or deaths feel random.
Several builders and one finisher on a single kill need clear credit for each.

variants.name: Shared charge
variants.summary: Builder weapons on any card add pips to enemy vehicles; full pips overload the vehicle, and finisher weapons hit an overloaded vehicle for heavy bonus damage. The basic version.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Tempest Charge, Tempest Overflow and Voltaic Reaction

variants.name: Affinity bonus
variants.summary: No overload at all: charged targets simply take extra damage from affinity weapons, so the pips are a soft mark rather than a lockout. The gentle version for low spice.

adds_strengths.why: Its hits charge enemy vehicles, and every charged vehicle takes extra damage from affinity weapons on its team.

adds_weaknesses.why: The charge never stops a vehicle or its abilities; it only adds damage, and soldiers and buildings ignore it.

variants.name: Charge and cash in
variants.summary: One card does both jobs: its main weapon lays pips, and a slower finisher shot on a key cashes in the overload, so a lone player can complete the combo, slowly.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Machinist (Searchlight Sensor builds Charge, Tempest Arc has Voltaic Reaction)

variants.name: Overload shot
variants.summary: A single heavy shot, usually from stealth or long range, overloads a vehicle at once without any pips, setting it up for any finisher on the team.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising GDF Sniper's shot from stealth and the Tempest Instability Missile

variants.name: Charge field
variants.summary: A pulse or field around the unit adds pips to every enemy vehicle inside it, so it charges a whole column without aiming.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Tempest Pulse (Cultivator) and Tempest fields

variants.name: Ignite burst
variants.summary: At full stacks the target bursts instead of locking up: an explosion hurts it and everything near it, the meter resets, and in some versions the burst spreads stacks to the targets it catches.
variants.seen_in: Destiny 2 Scorch and Ignition, Monster Hunter blastblight

variants.name: Stagger window
variants.summary: Any weapon fills a stagger gauge; at full the target is helpless for a moment and every hit on it does bonus damage, rewarding a team that saves its heavy shots for the window.
variants.seen_in: Armored Core VI ACS overload and Direct Hit damage

variants.name: Curse rallies attackers
variants.summary: The overloaded target is cursed: it is silenced and slowed, and every ally who hits it attacks faster while the curse lasts, so the whole team piles on.
variants.seen_in: Dota 2 Abaddon's Curse of Avernus (patches 7.20 to 7.35)

variants.name: Heat to shutdown
variants.summary: The stacks are heat. Builders can fill the target only to just below its limit, so it shuts down only if its own firing adds the rest: a trap that punishes a careless shooter.
variants.seen_in: MechWarrior Online flamer heat cap; tabletop BattleTech flamers

variants.name: Outright execution
variants.summary: As in Tempest Rising: a finisher hit destroys an overloaded vehicle outright, whatever its health or armour.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Voltaic Reaction (Voltaic Tank, Operative, Machinist)

adds_strengths.why: Its finisher hit destroys any overloaded vehicle outright, whatever its health or armour.
Its hits charge enemy vehicles, slowing them more with each pip; a full charge overloads them, and a finisher on the team turns the overload into a kill.

adds_weaknesses.why: Does little alone: the pips need many hits or teammates to fill, soldiers and buildings are immune, and only a finisher turns an overload into a kill.

counters.why: Stacks slow enemy vehicles more with every hit and an overload takes their abilities away, so the team can run them down.
The overload ignores armour: a finisher hits an overloaded heavy tank just as hard as a light one.

countered_by.why: Soldiers can't be charged at all, so an infantry-heavy enemy leaves the card with only its base damage.
Shielded or overload-proof vehicles shrug off the stacks and the finisher alike.

open_questions: Should a finisher kill an overloaded vehicle outright, as in Tempest Rising, or only deal a heavy bonus hit?
How many pips, how fast do they drain, and how long is the immunity after an overload? This needs playtesting.
Should soldiers stay immune, as in Tempest Rising, keeping the combo an anti-vehicle tool?
Should the overload block weapons too, or only abilities as in Tempest Rising?
Should pips from different builders share one meter, so the combo is a team effort, or count per player?

shooter_fit.reason: A team combo with clear jobs, builders and finisher, that Destiny 2 and Armored Core VI already prove in action play; it fits once the outright kill is softened into a bonus hit and every overload is followed by immunity.
